text:
alex: quick question — if we split control plane into a 'sideplane' (local control agents in customer VPC) vs central cp over privatelink, how do we want to handle egress IP preservation for callbacks?
nisha: short version: two options — preserve src (SNAT-less) via peering/eni/ip-aliasing, or SNAT at our edge and present a stable egress IP. both have ops/cost tradeoffs.
linus: preserving src is ideal for customers that have IP allowlists, but it's operationally expensive and brittle across region failover. route propagation + ENI mapping becomes a pain.
nash (infra-bot): deploy-check: sideplane agents currently support advertising 10.0.0.0/16 via BGP? false. need spike. :robot_face:
alex: right, so proposal: for sideplane we implement a lightweight static NAT gateway per-tenant (ephemeral egress) that can be pinned when customer requests static IP. default keeps SNAT at regional relay to simplify.
olivia: question — does pinning static IP mean reserved ENIs and VPC endpoint costs per customer? that could blow up costs at scale.
nisha: yes. pinning = reserved ENI+elastic IP (or equivalent in cloud). but we can offer an aggregated pool model: small set of shared static IPs per region + tenant header mapping for identification. not perfect for strict allowlists.
linus: mapping header doesn't help customers with network-level allowlists tho. we should gate strict src-preserve to enterprise + dedicated because of cost.
alex: agreed. can we do a hybrid fallback: prefer src-preserve when local ENI is available, otherwise fallback to shared static IP pool and add X-Redwood-Tenant header? fallback policy must be observable.
infra-bot: perf-check: estimated extra ~0.8ms p50 for per-tenant NAT path, batching unchanged. cost delta depends on EIP count.
olivia: rollout plan idea: start with sideplane feature-flag + beta tenants. default to regional SNAT; provide one-off migration for customers that need src-preserve. document network diagrams + failure modes.
nisha: also add a control-plane signal for 'egress-mode' in tenant config so routing + operator UI can show which mode used. makes audits easier.
linus: another concern — route convergence and blackhole windows during cp failover. if sideplane agent withdraws prefix, traffic might go to central relay and lose src-preserve. need soft-handoffs.
alex: implement a grace window on withdrawal (30s) and active-health-checked path switch. add a test harness simulating peering interruption.
olivia: test cases: allowlist acceptance test, failover maintains connectivity within SLO, metrics for IP-mapping count, and rollout smoke with 5 pilot tenants.
nisha: SLA and costing note: include explicit pricing for reserved egress IPs + operator runbook. engineering to produce an ops-runbook draft before beta.
alex: action items: linus spike BGP/route-propagation options (due +3d), infra to surface EIP cost estimate (infra-bot), olivia draft rollout + docs (due +7d). I'll open RFC followup with diagrams.
linus: acked. i'll add a small design doc snippet with failure diagrams.
infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-5234 "sideplane egress modes cost spike".
